new_articles.title: Intraportal implantation of hepatocytic spheroids enables effective engraftment and functional repopulation for liver failure treatment
new_articles.abstract: Hepatocyte transplantation for liver failure faces major challenges in acquiring sufficient functional hepatocytes and achieving high engraftment efficiency. Previously, we reprogrammed primary hepatocytes into hepatocyte-derived proliferative duct-like cells (HepPDCs) to resolve the shortage of donor cell sources. However, high-passage HepPDCs exhibit limited redifferentiation into functional hepatocytes, accompanied by inefficient liver repopulation in liver failure recipients. Here, we established a hepatic differentiation and maturation system for HepPDCs by constructing hepatocyte-derived proliferative duct-like cell spheroids (HPDCS) within a dynamic three-dimensional culture system containing hyaluronan. A two-stage differentiation protocol was developed to first induce HPDCS to form hepatocyte precursor-like cell spheroids (HPLCS) within 3 days, followed by terminal maturation into hepatocyte-like cell spheroids (HLCS) for an additional 9 days. Comparative analyses of the cellular phenotypes and molecular signatures of HPLCS and HLCS showed that both exhibited hepatic differentiation tendency and partial functionality, with HLCS presenting a more mature functional phenotype. Among the multiple additives used in the differentiation system, forskolin combined with dexamethasone were identified as key regulators driving the hepatic differentiation of HPDCS, a process closely associated with the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway that critically modulates hepatocyte differentiation and maturation. Portal vein transplantation of these hepatocytic spheroids (HPLCS and HLCS), combined with anticoagulant and anti-inflammatory interventions, enabled stable cell retention in portal venules for at least 14 days with sustained hepatic function. The transplanted spheroids subsequently crossed the endothelial barrier, underwent hepatic engraftment, facilitated liver regeneration, and supported long-term hepatic restoration. Collectively, this study established a promising strategy for treating liver failure through the intraportal transplantation of hepatocytic spheroids.

new_articles.title: The p53-YSC-YAP axis mediates enterocyte dedifferentiation during colonic regeneration after irradiation
new_articles.abstract: The intestinal epithelium is consistently exposed to various injuries and exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity. Although small intestinal regeneration has been extensively investigated, the mechanisms governing colonic regeneration remain poorly understood. Here, we identify irradiation-induced regenerative cells (IRECs), a previously unrecognized colonic enterocyte population that emerges following irradiation injury. IRECs, which are characterized by the expression of the YuanShangCao (Ysc) gene, undergo dedifferentiation and transition to a stem-like state, contributing to epithelial regeneration. IREC ablation severely impairs colonic repair. Mechanistically, YSC promotes colonic regeneration by preventing the lysosomal degradation of YAP. Furthermore, we demonstrate a critical role for p53 in colonic regeneration through the induction of Ysc expression. Together, our findings define IRECs as an irradiation injury-induced enterocyte population that dedifferentiates into stem cells during colonic epithelial repair and demonstrate that the p53-YSC-YAP axis plays a key role in this process, deepening the understanding of colonic diseases.

new_articles.title: ER–mitochondria contacts orchestrate mitochondrial transport via C19orf12
new_articles.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–mitochondria contact sites facilitate lipid transfer, calcium signaling, and mitochondrial division; however, their role in mitochondrial transport remains unclear. Here, we identify hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP)-associated protein C19orf12 as an ER-anchored regulator of mitochondrial trafficking. The loss of C19orf12 leads to perinuclear mitochondrial clustering in cells, impaired anterograde transport in neurons, and progressive locomotor dysfunction in mice that recapitulates key features of HSP in humans. Mechanistically, C19orf12 forms a discrete complex with the mitochondrial Rho GTPase Miro1 and the Kinesin-1 motor Kif5b, thereby providing a molecular link between ER–mitochondria contacts and microtubule-based anterograde transport. Ca2+ also modulated C19orf12–Miro1 behavior in vitro and showed a biphasic association with mitochondrial motility in live cells. Therefore, our findings establish ER‒mitochondria contact sites as logistical hubs for Kinesin-1 motor loading and highlight the importance of the Ca2+-tunable C19orf12 scaffold in sustaining directional mitochondrial transport, providing a mechanistic framework for how C19orf12 loss may contribute to neurodegeneration.
